Air Cond and Press.q: What happens to the APU Bleed when you select the APU BLD Pb?
What does the Crossbleed Valve do when you select the APU BLD Pb?
What do the Engine Bleed Valves do when you select the APU BLD Pb?
If the APU Bleed is left on during climb, at what altitude does it automatically close?
After closing automatically in the climb, at what altitude does the APU Bleed reopen in descent?
With the Crossbleed Valve in AUTO, Engines on and APU bleed OFF, what is the normal Crossbleed valve position?
When does the Crossbleed Valve move automatically?
Air Cond and Press.a: Only when the APU BLD valve opens or closes.

Air Cond and Press.q: When do we manually open or close the Crossbleed Valve?
What controls the Packs?
Air Cond and Press.a: The Pack Controllers, one Pack Controller per pack.

Air Cond and Press.q: How many Pack Controllers are there per pack?
If a Pack Controller fails, between what temperatures is the Pack outlet temperature regulated?
What regulates the temperature in the aircraft?
How many zone controllers and channels are there?
If the zone controller fails, to what temperature is the aircraft regulated?
What does the Pack Flow Selector regulate?
What pack flow does the LOW position of the Pack Flow Selector give?
In AUTO pack flow, where is the Passenger Count entered?
Air Cond and Press.a: On the INIT A page in the MCDU.

Air Cond and Press.q: In AUTO pack flow, what is airflow automatically adjusted on?
What pack flow does the HIGH position of the Pack Flow Selector give?
For what conditions is HIGH pack flow used?
When do the packs go to 125% flow?
Air Cond and Press.a: When the APU Bleed is ON, or for Single Pack operations.

Air Cond and Press.q: Where is the HOT AIR system air tapped from?
Which temperatures does the HOT AIR system regulate via the trim air valves?
Air Cond and Press.a: Cockpit, Cabin, and FWD cargo temperatures.

Air Cond and Press.q: What heats and what cools the Forward Cargo compartment?
Air Cond and Press.a: Heated by Hot Air 1, cooled by Pack 2.

Air Cond and Press.q: What primarily heats the Cockpit?
How are the valves in the Air Conditioning system controlled and operated?
Air Cond and Press.a: All electrically controlled and pneumatically operated.

Air Cond and Press.q: What temperature control range does the Flight Attendant CIDS panel have?
On what is the Flight Attendant CIDS panel temperature range centered?
Air Cond and Press.a: The Cabin temperature setting in the Cockpit.

Air Cond and Press.q: Where is the RAM AIR scoop located?
Air Cond and Press.a: On the lower left side of the fuselage.

Air Cond and Press.q: In what failure case can the RAM AIR scoop provide air into the cabin?
Which QRH checklist uses the RAM AIR scoop?
When will the RAM AIR Pb not function?
Air Cond and Press.a: When the Ditching Pb is selected.

Air Cond and Press.q: At what ∆P will the RAM AIR system open?
What do the outflow valves do when the Ditching Pb is selected on with the Press Mode Selector in AUTO?
What do the Cargo Isolation Valves do when the Ditching Pb is selected on?
What does the Ram Air Inlet do when the Ditching Pb is selected on?
What does the Avionics Ventilation Overboard Valve do when the Ditching Pb is selected on?
What do the Pack Flow Control Valves do when the Ditching Pb is selected on?
What are the two normal uses of the Ditching Pb?
Which cabin pressurization mode is the normal mode of operation?
How many CPCs (Cabin Pressure Controllers) are there?
How many outflow valves are there, and how many motors does each use in AUTO mode?
Air Cond and Press.a: 2 Outflow valves, each with 2 motors for the AUTO modes.

Air Cond and Press.q: In AUTO mode, where does the pressurization system get the landing elevation?
Air Cond and Press.a: FMGC provided landing elevation for the entered destination.

Air Cond and Press.q: When is the SEMI-AUTOMATIC pressurization mode used?
Air Cond and Press.a: When operating at an airport not in the database.

Air Cond and Press.q: In SEMI-AUTOMATIC mode, how is the destination elevation set?
Which CPCs and motors does SEMI-AUTOMATIC mode use?
Air Cond and Press.a: The same two CPCs and motors as the auto mode.

Air Cond and Press.q: In MANUAL pressurization mode, which controls are used to adjust pressurization?
Air Cond and Press.a: MODE SEL to Manual, then VALVE SEL and V/S CTL per ECAM procedure.

Air Cond and Press.q: In MANUAL pressurization mode, where are the target cabin altitudes provided?
Air Cond and Press.a: In the FCOM and on the STS page.

Air Cond and Press.q: Which outflow valve motor is used for Manual mode?
Air Cond and Press.a: A third motor on each Outflow valve.

Air Cond and Press.q: In MANUAL mode, how much change does each toggle of the V/S CTL give?
What circulates the air that cools the avionics?
On the ground, where is the avionics cooling air exhausted?
Air Cond and Press.a: Out of the OVBD Extract Valve.

Air Cond and Press.q: What happens to the OVBD Extract Valve and Underfloor Extract Valve at first engine start?
Air Cond and Press.a: The OVBD Extract Valve closes and the Underfloor Extract Valve opens.

Air Cond and Press.q: After first engine start, where does the avionics cooling air exit the aircraft?
Air Cond and Press.a: Under the Forward Cargo compartment and out the Forward Outflow Valve.

Air Cond and Press.q: What does the Underfloor Extract Valve do when the EXTRACT Pb is selected to OVRD?
What does the OVBD Extract Valve do when the EXTRACT Pb is selected to OVRD?
Air Cond and Press.a: It opens partially, using a separate small portion of the door.

Air Cond and Press.q: Which ECAM procedures most likely call for selecting the EXTRACT Pb to OVRD?
Air Cond and Press.a: Vent Extract Fault or Vent OVBD Valve Fault.

Air Cond and Press.q: What is the source of air for the Cargo compartments?
What is the top row of the CARGO AIR COND panel?
What is the middle row of the CARGO AIR COND panel?
What is the bottom row of the CARGO AIR COND panel?
What happens to the Isolation Valves when a compartment Isolation Valve Pb is selected to Off?
Air Cond and Press.a: The Inlet and Outlet Isolation Valves close.

Air Cond and Press.q: What happens to the Extract Fan when a compartment Isolation Valve Pb is selected to Off?
With the Isolation Valve Pbs ON, when do the isolation valves automatically close?
Air Cond and Press.a: When Cargo Smoke is detected or the Ditching Pb is selected ON.

Air Cond and Press.q: What cools the forward cargo compartment?
What heats the forward cargo compartment?
What is the memory phrase for forward cargo heating and cooling?
Air Cond and Press.a: Heated from the left, Cooled from the right.

Air Cond and Press.q: What does the temperature selector knob below the cargo cooling selector control?
Air Cond and Press.a: The trim air valve on the Hot Air 1 system.

Air Cond and Press.q: Can the Aft cargo compartment be heated or cooled?
Air Cond and Press.a: No. It cannot be heated or cooled.

Air Cond and Press.q: How is the Bulk cargo compartment heated?
When does the Bulk cargo compartment heater activate?
Air Cond and Press.a: When the temperature falls below the set level.

Air Cond and Press.q: What does the Bulk cargo heater do once the set temperature level is reached?
Air Cond and Press.a: It shuts off until the temperature falls again.

Air Cond and Press.q: What Bulk temperature do we set when live animals are carried in the Bulk compartment?
What is the normal position of the FWD CARGO COOLING selector?
Air Cond and Press.a: OFF, unless plants, livestock, or foods are carried.

Air Cond and Press.q: Which carried items require the FWD CARGO COOLING selector to be on?
In which compartment are pets carried?

Auto Flight.q: Which QRH reset table is used to reset a blank or locked MCDU?
Auto Flight.a: The QRH reset table (02.02D) and related procedures.

Auto Flight.q: How can a blank or locked MCDU be turned off?
Auto Flight.a: By pressing and holding the DIM key.

Auto Flight.q: Which MCDU can be used as a replacement after a failed MCDU is turned off?
Auto Flight.a: MCDU 3.

Auto Flight.q: Below what altitude do the Autoland Lights become active in LAND mode?
Auto Flight.a: Below 200 ft RA.

Auto Flight.q: What is the action if the Autoland lights begin flashing?
Auto Flight.a: Go Around.

Auto Flight.q: When do mode reversions occur?
Auto Flight.a: When the pilot asks the FMGEC to perform a task it is unable to do.

Auto Flight.q: What does the FMGEC do during a mode reversion?
Auto Flight.a: It reverts to a simpler mode to ensure a safe flight path.

Auto Flight.q: What aural cue is heard when a mode reversion occurs?
Auto Flight.a: A triple click, click click click, think Look Look Look.

Auto Flight.q: During a managed climb in CLB and NAV, what does CLB revert to when HDG is selected?
Auto Flight.a: OP CLB.

Auto Flight.q: During a managed descent in DES and NAV, what does DES revert to when HDG is selected?
Auto Flight.a: V/S.

Auto Flight.q: When climbing or descending with ALT* engaged, what happens if a different altitude is selected?
Auto Flight.a: ALT* reverts to V/S.

Auto Flight.q: What happens when an altitude opposite to the direction of flight is set in the FCU?
Auto Flight.a: The vertical mode reverts to V/S.

Auto Flight.q: What does NAV revert to when overflying a route discontinuity?
Auto Flight.a: HDG.

Auto Flight.q: With the FDs on in a climb and the pilot leveling off without following them, to what speed does the aircraft accelerate?
Auto Flight.a: Vmax.

Auto Flight.q: In a climb with FDs on, what happens to the FDs and A/THR when Vmax is reached?
Auto Flight.a: Both FDs disengage and A/THR reverts to SPEED.

Auto Flight.q: In a climb with FDs on, what does A/THR do to thrust after reverting to SPEED at Vmax?
Auto Flight.a: Reduces thrust to recover the speed target.

Auto Flight.q: With the FDs on in a descent and the pilot leveling off without following them, to what speed does the aircraft decelerate?
Auto Flight.a: Vls.

Auto Flight.q: In a descent with FDs on, what happens to the FDs and A/THR when Vls is reached?
Auto Flight.a: Both FDs disengage and A/THR reverts to SPEED.

Auto Flight.q: In a descent with FDs on, what does A/THR do to thrust after reverting to SPEED at Vls?
Auto Flight.a: Increases thrust to recover the speed target.

Auto Flight.q: How many Autothrust computers and channels are there?
Auto Flight.a: 1 Autothrust computer with 2 channels, one channel per FMGEC.

Auto Flight.q: How is switching between Autothrust channels accomplished?
Auto Flight.a: By switching autopilots.

Auto Flight.q: What is the Match and Mash method of turning off the Autothrust inflight?
Auto Flight.a: Match TLA on the EPR gauges to current thrust, then press the Instinctive Disconnect Pb.

Auto Flight.q: What happens if the Instinctive Disconnect Pb is pressed and held for 15 seconds?
Auto Flight.a: The Autothrust is removed for the remainder of the flight.

Auto Flight.q: What protection is lost when the Autothrust is removed for the remainder of the flight?
Auto Flight.a: Alpha Floor protection.

Auto Flight.q: What is the Non-Standard method of turning off the Autothrust?
Auto Flight.a: Retard the thrust levers to IDLE, then press the Autothrust Pb on the FCU.

Auto Flight.q: What condition results from the Non-Standard method of turning off the Autothrust?
Auto Flight.a: A Thrust Lock condition until the Thrust Levers are moved manually.

Auto Flight.q: On takeoff, what arms the Autothrust?
Auto Flight.a: Moving the Thrust Levers to Flex or TOGA.

Auto Flight.q: What flashes on the FMA at THR RED altitude?
Auto Flight.a: LVR CLB.

Auto Flight.q: On takeoff, what activates the Autothrust?
Auto Flight.a: Moving the Thrust Levers to CLB.

Auto Flight.q: In flight, what activates the Autothrust?
Auto Flight.a: Pressing the A/THR Pb.

Auto Flight.q: After pressing the A/THR Pb in flight, how long does LVR CLB flash on the FMA?
Auto Flight.a: Until the Thrust Levers are in the climb detent.

Auto Flight.q: What is Groundspeed Mini designed to protect the aircraft from?
Auto Flight.a: Windshear on approach.

Auto Flight.q: What does Groundspeed Mini attempt to maintain during the approach?
Auto Flight.a: A minimum energy level throughout the approach during variable wind conditions.

Auto Flight.q: What must be engaged for Groundspeed Mini?
Auto Flight.a: Managed speed.

Auto Flight.q: Is Autothrust required for Groundspeed Mini?
Auto Flight.a: No. Autothrust is not required.

Auto Flight.q: What FMA is displayed on takeoff?
Auto Flight.a: MAN FLEX __ | SRS | RWY | | A/THR.

Auto Flight.q: When does RWY appear on the takeoff FMA?
Auto Flight.a: Only if there is an ILS for that runway.

Auto Flight.q: What color is A/THR on the takeoff FMA, and what does it signify?
Auto Flight.a: Blue, meaning armed.

Auto Flight.q: What FMA is displayed for an RNAV climb?
Auto Flight.a: THR CLB | CLB | NAV | | A/THR.

Auto Flight.q: What FMA is displayed in a vectored descent?
Auto Flight.a: THR IDLE | OP DES | HDG | | A/THR.

Auto Flight.q: What FMA is displayed in a NAV descent?
Auto Flight.a: THR IDLE or THR DES | DES | NAV | | A/THR.

Auto Flight.q: What FMA is displayed on an ILS APP?
Auto Flight.a: SPEED | GS | LOC | CAT3/DUAL | 1AP2.

Auto Flight.q: What is the highest landing capability of the aircraft?
Auto Flight.a: CAT 3 DUAL.

Auto Flight.q: What is the highest landing capability when single engine?
Auto Flight.a: CAT 3 SINGLE.

Auto Flight.q: What does 1 FD 2 on the FMA mean?
Auto Flight.a: Normal mode of operation, both FDs selected on.

Auto Flight.q: What does 1 FD on the FMA mean?
Auto Flight.a: FD 2 is not selected on.

Auto Flight.q: What does 1 FD 1 on the FMA mean?
Auto Flight.a: FD 2 has failed.

Auto Flight.q: What does SRS stand for?
Auto Flight.a: Speed Reference System.

Auto Flight.q: How does SRS deliver a speed?
Auto Flight.a: It uses vertical guidance to deliver a speed.

Auto Flight.q: What speed does SRS target on a normal takeoff?
What speed does SRS target on a go around?
Auto Flight.a: The highest of Vapp or the current speed at Go Around.

Auto Flight.q: What speed does SRS target single engine?
Auto Flight.a: The highest of V2 or the airspeed at failure.

Comms and Cabin Systems.q: What must illuminate during a CVR test?
During preflight, to what position is the PA reception knob set?
Why is the PA reception knob set to the 12 o'clock position during preflight?
Comms and Cabin Systems.a: So the CVR records any PA transmissions.

Comms and Cabin Systems.q: What can be used as a replacement if ACP 1 or ACP 2 fails?
Which control selects ACP 3 as a replacement for a failed ACP?
Comms and Cabin Systems.a: The AUDIO SWITCHING knob on the switching panel.

Comms and Cabin Systems.q: What does the ALL call do?
Comms and Cabin Systems.a: CALL ALL CAPT appears on all FA panels.

Comms and Cabin Systems.q: What does the MECH call activate?
Comms and Cabin Systems.a: A horn in the nose wheel well and a light on the external power panel.

Comms and Cabin Systems.q: How long does the MECH call light remain illuminated?
Comms and Cabin Systems.a: Until reset by ground crew on the external power panel.

Comms and Cabin Systems.q: What does the CAB REST call do?
What do the FWD, MID, EXIT and AFT calls do?
What does the EVAC switch activate?
Is the EVAC alert used per HAL procedure?
Comms and Cabin Systems.a: No. It is not used per HAL procedure.

Comms and Cabin Systems.q: During preflight, in what position do we verify the EVAC switch?
What does the EVAC switch in the CAPT position ensure?
Comms and Cabin Systems.a: The Flight Attendants cannot activate the Alert Audio.

Comms and Cabin Systems.q: Besides the cockpit switch, where is there an EVAC Pb?
How many lights are on the Cockpit Door Overhead Control Panel?
What does an illuminated light on the Cockpit Door Overhead Control Panel indicate?
Comms and Cabin Systems.a: The corresponding door latch is faulty.

Electrical.q: What is the power hierarchy for AC BUS 1?
Electrical.a: Generator 1, APU Generator, External B, External A, Generator 2.

Electrical.q: What is the power hierarchy for AC BUS 2?
Electrical.a: Generator 2, External A, APU Generator, External B, Generator 1.

Electrical.q: Which source powers AC BUS 1 if Generator 1 is unavailable?
Electrical.a: The APU Generator.

Electrical.q: Which source powers AC BUS 2 if Generator 2 is unavailable?
Electrical.a: External A.

Electrical.q: When External A indicates AVAIL, what is powered regardless of the switch position?
Electrical.a: The GND SRV Bus.

Electrical.q: What happens when the External A Pb is selected ON?
Electrical.a: External power connects to the rest of the system based on the power hierarchy.

Electrical.q: What does the External B Pb display when selected with External B AVAIL?
Electrical.a: AUTO.

Electrical.q: Under what condition will External B connect with the system?
Electrical.a: Provided the APU Generator is not online.

Electrical.q: What does the AUTO indication on the External B Pb signify?
Electrical.a: It connects and disconnects automatically based on the APU Generator status.

Electrical.q: What normally powers the AC ESS BUS?
Electrical.a: AC BUS 1.

Electrical.q: If AC BUS 1 is lost, what powers the AC ESS BUS?
Electrical.a: AC BUS 2 via the ESS XFEED.

Electrical.q: What happens when ALTN is selected on the ESS XFEED Pb?
Electrical.a: AC BUS 2 powers the AC ESS BUS.

Electrical.q: During Initial Power Up, what should the battery voltage be above?
What battery charge does 25.5V represent?
Electrical.a: 50% charge on the Batteries.

Electrical.q: What do we do if the battery charge is lower than 25.5V at Initial Power Up?
Electrical.a: Charge off external power for 20 minutes and check again.

Electrical.q: Below what APU battery voltage is there a risk of an aborted APU start on battery only?
How do we check the battery voltages?
Electrical.a: Select BAT 1, BAT 2, APU BAT Pbs off, read the Voltage Indicator window, switch batteries with the selector.

Electrical.q: In what position is the battery selector left after checking battery voltages?
Electrical.a: The APU BAT position.

Electrical.q: What may not be available if the main batteries were low prior to an APU start on battery power?
Electrical.a: The APU fire protection.

Electrical.q: Which ECAM page is selected to check the Battery Charge Limiter during preflight?
Electrical.a: The ELEC DC page.

Electrical.q: What switching sequence is used to check the Battery Charge Limiter?
Electrical.a: Turn off BAT 1, BAT 2, and APU BAT, then turn them back on.

Electrical.q: What battery draw verifies the Battery Charge Limiter is functioning properly?
Electrical.a: Less than 60 amps in 10 seconds or less.

Electrical.q: How long can we operate on batteries only?
Electrical.a: A minimum of 30 minutes.

Electrical.q: What does the GALLEY Pb AUTO position (lights out) indicate?
Electrical.a: The galley will automatically shed in case of failures.

Electrical.q: What does the COMMERCIAL Pb control?
Electrical.a: Everything back of the Cockpit door (Galley, IFE, Cargo loading, etc.).

Electrical.q: How long, at most, should the IDG disconnect be held?
Electrical.a: Not greater than 3 seconds.

Electrical.q: Why should the IDG disconnect not be held for greater than 3 seconds?
Electrical.a: The disconnect mechanism could be damaged.

Electrical.q: Can the IDG be reconnected in flight?
Electrical.a: No. The IDG cannot be reconnected in flight.

Electrical.q: Which items connect to the Hot Battery bus on the ground and remain powered at all times?
Electrical.a: The Clock and the Battery Voltage Indication Window.

Electrical.q: What is the EMER GEN TEST used for?
Electrical.a: A maintenance function only.

Electrical.q: What does the EMER ELEC PWR panel label refer to?
Electrical.a: The Emergency Generator.

Electrical.q: Where is the EMER ELEC CONFIG summary located?
Electrical.a: In the QRH.

Electrical.q: What is powering the aircraft when it is in EMER ELEC CONFIG?
Electrical.a: The Emergency Generator, with many electrical items shed.

Electrical.q: Which hydraulic system powers the Emergency Generator?
Electrical.a: The green hydraulic system, via two methods.

Electrical.q: What powers the green system in the “Big Green” case?
Electrical.a: One or both engine driven pumps.

Electrical.q: What powers the green system in the “Little Green” case?
Electrical.a: The RAT only.

Electrical.q: What percentage of an engine driven pump flow capability can the RAT provide?
Electrical.a: Between 15% and 45%, depending on airspeed.

Electrical.q: Loss of which two busses automatically activates EMER ELEC CONFIG?
Electrical.a: AC Bus 1 and AC Bus 2, with both Engine Generators tripped offline.

Electrical.q: After loss of AC Bus 1 and AC Bus 2, what powers the Emergency Generator?
Electrical.a: Big Green hydraulics.

Electrical.q: How many busses remain powered in EMER ELEC CONFIG after loss of AC Bus 1 and AC Bus 2?
Electrical.a: 4 busses.

Electrical.q: Which 4 busses remain powered in EMER ELEC CONFIG after loss of AC Bus 1 and AC Bus 2?
Electrical.a: AC ESS, AC ESS SHED, DC ESS, DC ESS SHED.

Electrical.q: Which displays remain in EMER ELEC CONFIG after loss of AC Bus 1 and AC Bus 2?
Electrical.a: Captains PFD, Captains ND, and E/WD.

Electrical.q: After loss of both engines, what powers the Emergency Generator?
Electrical.a: Little Green (the RAT only).

Electrical.q: How many busses remain powered in EMER ELEC CONFIG after loss of both engines?
Electrical.a: 2 busses.

Electrical.q: Which 2 busses remain powered in EMER ELEC CONFIG after loss of both engines?
Electrical.a: AC ESS and DC ESS.

Electrical.q: Which displays remain in EMER ELEC CONFIG after loss of both engines?
Electrical.a: Captains PFD and E/WD.

Electrical.q: Can the emergency generator be turned on manually?
Electrical.a: Yes. It can also be manually turned on.

Electrical.q: Once the emergency generator has been turned on, can it be turned off?
Electrical.a: No. It cannot be turned off.

Electrical.q: When does a RAT-powered emergency generator disconnect?
Electrical.a: When the slats are extended.

Electrical.q: How is the RAT-powered emergency generator reactivated after slat extension disconnects it?
Electrical.a: Push the MAN ON Pb after the slats have been retracted.

Electrical.q: Below what airspeed does the RAT stop being effective?
Electrical.a: Less than 140 kts.

Electrical.q: What is the only source of power once the RAT stops being effective below 140 kts?
Electrical.a: The batteries.

Electrical.q: What happens to the Land Recovery AC and DC busses when the aircraft enters EMER ELEC CONFIG?
Electrical.a: They shed.

Electrical.q: What kind of systems are on the Land Recovery busses?
Electrical.a: Systems required for landing but not during cruise.

Electrical.q: Do the Land Recovery busses recover automatically if normal power is restored?
Electrical.a: No. They remain shed even if normal power is restored.

Electrical.q: What does the Land Recovery Pb do?
Electrical.a: Recovers the Land Recovery AC and DC busses, restoring systems required for landing.

Electrical.q: Which systems does the Land Recovery Pb restore when Big Green powers the Emergency Generator?
Electrical.a: LGCIU 1, SFCC 1, BSCU CH 1, LH Windshield Heat, LH Landing Light.

Electrical.q: Which systems does the Land Recovery Pb restore when Little Green powers the Emergency Generator?
Electrical.a: LGCIU 1 and SFCC 1 (slat channel only).

Electrical.q: Are the reset panel switches circuit breakers?
Electrical.a: No. They are computer reset switches.

Electrical.q: Where is the explanation of the reset procedures found?
Electrical.a: The first page of the reset sections in both the FCOM and QRH.

Electrical.q: When can you accomplish a computer reset as directed?
Electrical.a: When instructed by an ECAM or paper QRH procedure.

Electrical.q: If no ECAM or QRH procedure directs a reset, how do you determine whether one is allowed?
Electrical.a: Check the QRH table.

Electrical.q: How are system Pbs that also function as resets marked?
Electrical.a: Noted by /R.

Electrical.q: Which two cockpit switches are also resets?
Electrical.a: The MCDU and A/SKID & N/W STRG (BSCU) switches.

Electrical.q: How many circuit breakers are in the cockpit?
Electrical.a: Only 5.

Electrical.q: Where are the 5 cockpit circuit breakers located?
Electrical.a: 3 on the cockpit door frame, 1 under each pilot seat on the pedestal.

Electrical.q: With the Emergency Exit Light switch armed, what conditions bring the lights on?
Electrical.a: Normal electrical power fails, DC ESS Bus fails, AC BUS 1 fails, or cabin altitude over 9550 ft.

Electrical.q: Which emergency lights come on when AC BUS 1 fails with the exit lights armed?
Electrical.a: Only the overhead emergency lights, to provide minimum lighting.

Electrical.q: At what cabin altitude do the EXIT signs come on with the exit lights armed?
Electrical.a: Over 9550 ft.

Electrical.q: When are the Fasten Seat Belt signs on in the Auto position?
Electrical.a: When either the gear is extended, or the flaps/slats are not at 0.

Electrical.q: Why are the No Smoking lights always on?
Electrical.a: They are hardwired.

Electrical.q: What else comes on when the No Smoking switch is in the ON position?
Electrical.a: The EXIT signs.

Electrical.q: What happens if the No Smoking switch is left ON after all power is shut off?
Electrical.a: The EXIT sign internal batteries would be depleted. Turned off in the Securing Checklist.

Electrical.q: What is the No Smoking switch used to signal to the Flight Attendants?
Electrical.a: Passing through 10000 ft.

Fire Protection.q: What type of fire detection loops do the engines use?
Fire Protection.a: Gas detection loops, the same as the APU.

Fire Protection.q: How many gas filled fire detection loops does each engine have?
How does a gas filled fire detection loop sense a fire?
Fire Protection.a: Heated gas expands and sets off a sensor at a predetermined level.

Fire Protection.q: Is an engine fire warning issued when both loops detect a fire?
Fire Protection.a: Yes. Both loops detecting a fire issues a warning.

Fire Protection.q: Is an engine fire warning issued when one loop detects a fire and the other is inoperative?
Fire Protection.a: Yes. One loop detecting fire with the other inoperative issues a warning.

Fire Protection.q: Within what time must both engine loops break to issue a fire warning?
What happens to the engine fire warnings if the fire goes out?
How many Halon bottles are there per engine?
What happens to the CRC when the ENG FIRE Pb is pushed?
What does pushing the ENG FIRE Pb do to the FADEC?
What does pushing the ENG FIRE Pb do to the SQUIBS?
Which hydraulic and fuel valves close when the ENG FIRE Pb is pushed?
Fire Protection.a: The Hydraulic Fire Shutoff Valve and the Low-Pressure Fuel Valve.

Fire Protection.q: What does pushing the ENG FIRE Pb do to the IDG?
Which pneumatic valves close when the ENG FIRE Pb is pushed?
Fire Protection.a: The Pack Flow Control Valve and the Engine Bleed Valve.

Fire Protection.q: What aural and master warning indications occur during the Engine Fire Test?
Fire Protection.a: The CRC sounds and the Master Warning lights flash.

Fire Protection.q: Which Pb lights come on during the Engine Fire Test?
Fire Protection.a: The Engine Fire Pbs and the SQUIB and DISCH lights.

Fire Protection.q: Where do fire lights come on near the pedestal during the Engine Fire Test?
How does the ENG 1 FIRE ECAM presentation differ from ENG 2 FIRE during the Engine Fire Test?
Fire Protection.a: ENG 1 FIRE appears on the left with checklist, ENG 2 FIRE on the right as title only.

Fire Protection.q: How many lights in total illuminate during the Engine Fire Test?
Fire Protection.a: 12 lights (including 2 ECAM messages), plus the CRC.

Fire Protection.q: What controls the automatic functions of the APU?
What happens automatically in case of an APU fire on the ground?
Does automatic APU shutdown and fire extinguishing occur if the APU fire happens airborne?
Fire Protection.a: No. It will not happen airborne.

Fire Protection.q: How many Halon bottles does the APU have?
How many gas filled fire detection loops does the APU have?
Under what three conditions is an APU fire warning issued?
Fire Protection.a: Both loops detect fire, one detects with the other inoperative, or both break within 5 seconds.

Fire Protection.q: What happens to the APU fire warnings if the fire goes out?
What happens to the APU itself when the APU FIRE Pb is pushed?
What happens to the CRC and squib when the APU FIRE Pb is pushed?
Fire Protection.a: The CRC is silenced and the squib is armed.

Fire Protection.q: Which fuel items are affected when the APU FIRE Pb is pushed?
Fire Protection.a: The LP Fuel Valve closes and the APU Fuel Pumps (FWD and AFT) shut off.

Fire Protection.q: What happens to the APU generator when the APU FIRE Pb is pushed?
Which pneumatic valves close when the APU FIRE Pb is pushed?
Fire Protection.a: The APU bleed valve and the Crossbleed valve.

Fire Protection.q: Which lights and messages appear when the APU fire test Pb is pushed?
Fire Protection.a: APU FIRE Pb, AGENT SQUIB and DISCH Pb lights, 2 Master Warnings, CRC, E/WD APU FIRE message.

Fire Protection.q: How many Master Warning lights illuminate during the APU fire test?
What is the total item count by color during the APU fire test?
Fire Protection.a: 4 red lights/messages, 1 amber light, 1 white light, and the CRC.

Fire Protection.q: What type of detectors does Avionics Smoke detection use?
What type of smoke detectors does the Cargo Smoke system use?
Why is it not possible to tell if a cargo fire has been extinguished?
Fire Protection.a: Remaining particulates and Halon in the compartment keep the optical detectors sensing.

Fire Protection.q: How many Halon bottles does the cargo fire extinguishing system have?
Fire Protection.a: 2 bottles, both discharging into the selected compartment.

Fire Protection.q: How quickly does the first cargo Halon bottle discharge?
How is the second cargo Halon bottle released?
How long does the second cargo Halon bottle take to fully discharge?
Why does the second cargo Halon bottle discharge over 260 minutes?
When does the cargo bottle DISCH light illuminate?
Fire Protection.a: Not until the bottle is fully empty.

Fire Protection.q: Which Pb controls cargo fire extinguishing for the Bulk compartment?
Fire Protection.a: The Aft Pb. The bottles discharge into both the Aft and Bulk compartments.

Fire Protection.q: What is the cargo smoke Test button used for?

Flight Controls.q: How many PRIMs does the aircraft have?
Flight Controls.a: 3 PRIMs, used for Normal, Alternate, and Direct Laws.

Flight Controls.q: How many SECs does the aircraft have?
Flight Controls.a: 2 SECs, used for Direct Law if no PRIMs are working.

Flight Controls.q: Which flight control law do the SECs provide if no PRIMs are working?
Flight Controls.a: Direct Law.

Flight Controls.q: Are the FCC Pbs reset switches?
Flight Controls.a: Yes. All FCC Pbs are reset switches.

Flight Controls.q: How many flight control computers are needed to perform a safe landing?
Flight Controls.a: Only 1 computer of any type.

Flight Controls.q: On which SD page are the speedbrakes displayed?
Flight Controls.a: The F/CTL page.

Flight Controls.q: Which spoiler panels are used for speedbrakes and ground spoilers?
Flight Controls.a: All the panels. Only some are used for roll control.

Flight Controls.q: Can the speedbrakes be used with Full flaps?
Flight Controls.a: Yes. The speedbrakes can be used with Full flaps.

Flight Controls.q: Can the aircraft be landed with the speedbrakes extended?
Flight Controls.a: Yes. The aircraft can be landed with the speedbrakes extended.

Flight Controls.q: During an RTO, what conditions cause the ground spoilers to extend?
Flight Controls.a: Thrust levers retarded to idle with speed greater than 72 kts.

Flight Controls.q: When armed, what causes the ground spoilers to extend during landing?
Flight Controls.a: Main gear compression with the thrust levers at IDLE.

Flight Controls.q: When not armed, what causes the ground spoilers to extend during landing?
Flight Controls.a: Main gear compression with at least 1 engine in reverse.

Flight Controls.q: What do the ground spoilers do if only 1 main gear touches down with reverse selected on 1 engine?
Flight Controls.a: They partially extend until the second main gear touches down, then extend normally.

Flight Controls.q: Why do the ground spoilers only partially extend when one main gear touches down first?
Flight Controls.a: It allows a smoother touchdown in crosswind conditions.

Flight Controls.q: When can the rudder trim be manually adjusted?
Flight Controls.a: Only when the autopilot is off.

Flight Controls.q: What happens to the rudder trim knob and reset button when the autopilot is on?
Flight Controls.a: They do not function.

Flight Controls.q: Which computers control the TURB DAMP function?
Flight Controls.a: The PRIMs.

Flight Controls.q: What does the TURB DAMP function do?
Flight Controls.a: Dampens structural modes induced by atmospheric turbulence.

Flight Controls.q: When can TURB DAMP be turned off?
Flight Controls.a: If it is considered not to be helping comfort.

Flight Controls.q: What three parameters must be met for TURB DAMP to be active?
Flight Controls.a: In flight within normal envelope, Normal Law active or A/P engaged, airspeed greater than 200 kts.

Flight Controls.q: Above what airspeed is TURB DAMP active?
Flight Controls.a: Greater than 200 kts.

Flight Controls.q: How many pilots should make sidestick inputs at a time?
Flight Controls.a: Only one pilot.

Flight Controls.q: What happens to the inputs when both sidesticks are moved at the same time?
Flight Controls.a: The inputs are summed.

Flight Controls.q: What audio warning sounds when both sidesticks receive inputs at the same time?
Flight Controls.a: “Dual Input”.

Flight Controls.q: Which SIDE STICK PRIORITY lights illuminate during a dual input?
Flight Controls.a: Green “CAPT” and “FO” lights.

Flight Controls.q: How does a pilot take control of the sidesticks from the other pilot?
Flight Controls.a: Press and hold the red Pb on their sidestick.

Flight Controls.q: When both pilots press and hold their sidestick red Pb, who has priority?
Flight Controls.a: The last pilot to press and hold.

Flight Controls.q: For which pilot does the red arrow in the SIDE STICK PRIORITY light illuminate?
Flight Controls.a: The pilot who is no longer in control.

Flight Controls.q: What audio message accompanies a sidestick priority takeover?
Flight Controls.a: “Priority Left” or “Priority Right” as appropriate.

Flight Controls.q: How long must the red Pb be held to lock out the other pilot's sidestick for the remainder of the flight?
Flight Controls.a: More than 40 seconds.

Flight Controls.q: How can a deactivated sidestick be activated again?
Flight Controls.a: Push its red Pb.

Flight Controls.q: What does the green band on the THS wheel indicate?
Flight Controls.a: The certified limits.

Flight Controls.q: What does setting the pitch trim within the THS green band ensure?
Flight Controls.a: The aircraft can perform a safe takeoff.

Flight Controls.q: What does having the correct pitch trim setting provide?
Flight Controls.a: A consistent rotation.

Flight Controls.q: When is the Automatic Retraction System (ARS) used?
Flight Controls.a: Heavy weight operations when S speed is greater than or near the 1+F limit speed of 215 kts.

Flight Controls.q: At what speed does the ARS automatically retract the flaps?
Flight Controls.a: As the speed increases through 200 kts.

Flight Controls.q: What does the Flap Load Relief System do?
Flight Controls.a: Automatically retracts the flaps to the next retracted lever position in an overspeed.

Flight Controls.q: In Flaps 2, 3, or FULL, how much overspeed causes the flaps to retract one position?
Flight Controls.a: 2.5 kts overspeed.

Flight Controls.q: What is displayed on the PFD when the Flap Load Relief System is active?
Flight Controls.a: RELIEF, above the Slat/Flap indicator.

Flight Controls.q: When do the flaps reextend after a flap load relief retraction?
Flight Controls.a: After the aircraft slows to 2.5 kts below Vfe.

Flight Controls.q: What does the Alpha/Speed Lock inhibit?
Flight Controls.a: Slat retraction from 1 to 0.

Flight Controls.q: What speed or Alpha conditions activate the Alpha/Speed Lock?
Flight Controls.a: Speed below 148 kts or Alpha exceeding 8.5 degrees.

Flight Controls.q: What is displayed on the PFD when the Alpha/Speed Lock is active?
Flight Controls.a: LOCK, above the Slats/Flaps indicator.

Flight Controls.q: What conditions allow the slats to retract to 0 after an Alpha/Speed Lock?
Flight Controls.a: Alpha below 8.2 degrees and speed exceeding 154 kts.

Flight Controls.q: Why do the ailerons droop when the flaps are set at 1 or greater?
Flight Controls.a: To provide additional lift.

Flight Controls.q: How much do the ailerons droop at Flaps 1+F?
Flight Controls.a: 5 degrees.

Flight Controls.q: How much do the ailerons droop at Flaps 2 through Full?
Flight Controls.a: 10 degrees.

Flight Controls.q: Is there aileron droop when Flaps 1 is selected while airborne?
Flight Controls.a: No. No flaps are extended at Flaps 1 airborne, so there is no droop.

Fuel.q: How many Fuel Control and Monitoring Computers (FCMC) control the fuel system?
What is the approximate capacity of each outer tank?
What is the approximate capacity of each inner tank?
What is the approximate capacity of the tail tank?
What is the approximate capacity of the center tank?
What is the approximate total fuel capacity?
Which tanks fill first during refueling?
At around what total fuel load should fuel start going into the Trim tank?
At around what total fuel load should fuel start going into the Center tank?
From where do the engines draw their fuel?
In what order do the other tanks feed the INNER tank as fuel burns off?
Fuel.a: CENTER to INNER, then TRIM to INNER, then OUTER to INNER.

Fuel.q: What is the tail trim tank used for?
Why is the CG moved aft during cruise?
What effect does an aft CG have during takeoff?
Passing what flight level in the climb do the FCMCs start the aft transfer to the trim tank?
During cruise, why is trim tank fuel transferred forward as needed?
Fuel.a: To maintain Inner tank levels and optimum CG.

Fuel.q: When do the FCMCs begin the forward transfer of remaining trim tank fuel during descent?
Fuel.a: Passing FL 24.5, or when 35 minutes or less from destination.

Fuel.q: What does selecting FWD on the TTANK MODE Pb do?
Fuel.a: Manually transfers fuel from the TRIM tank to the CENTER tank.

Fuel.q: Which is the only fuel transfer Pb with a direction?
What happens with the TTANK Feed switch in the AUTO position?
Fuel.a: The FCMC automatically transfers fuel throughout the flight.

Fuel.q: Why is the final forward transfer stopped with a small amount of fuel left in the trim tank?
Fuel.a: So the trim tank transfer line contains fuel for APU operation.

Fuel.q: What does the OPEN position of the TTANK Feed switch do?
Fuel.a: Opens the valves to allow gravity feed to the center tank.

Fuel.q: What happens to the trim tank transfer line with the TTANK Feed switch in OPEN?
Fuel.a: It is drained, and the APU will not operate.

Fuel.q: What does the ISOL position of the TTANK Feed switch do?
What does the CTR TANK XFR Pb do?
Fuel.a: Performs a manual transfer from the Center tank to the Inner tanks.

Fuel.q: How much fuel is unusable if the Center tank pumps are inoperative?
Why is 33,000 lbs of center tank fuel unusable with the Center tank pumps inoperative?
Fuel.a: Due to gravity and wing dihedral.

Fuel.q: What does the OUTR TK XFR Pb do?
Fuel.a: Performs a gravity transfer from the Outer tanks to the Inner tanks by opening the valves.

Fuel.q: Can the engines suction feed fuel?
Fuel.a: Yes. They can suction feed from the collector tanks.

Fuel.q: What should be used to conduct all manual fuel transfers?
What protection is lost during manual fuel transfers?
Fuel.a: Overfill protections. Tanks could overfill and fuel could be lost overboard.

Fuel.q: When does the WING XFEED open automatically?
Fuel.a: During a fuel jettison and during EMER ELEC CONFIG.

Fuel.q: At around what fuel imbalance should you start checking the limitations chart?
At what fuel imbalance does the advisory come on?
Can the aircraft be flown and landed in any fuel imbalance scenario?
Fuel.a: Yes. In exceptional conditions, in any fuel imbalance scenario.

Fuel.q: What do the INR TANK SPLIT pushbuttons do?
Fuel.a: Close a valve in each Inner tank, closing the connection between the 2 parts of the tank.

Fuel.q: What is the normal position of the inner tank split valve?
What is the purpose of splitting the inner tank?
Fuel.a: To protect a portion of the inner tank fuel in case of a fuel leak.

Fuel.q: After an inner tank split, is all fuel still accessible?
Fuel.a: Yes. All fuel is still accessible via the main and standby pumps.

Fuel.q: Why are the INR TANK SPLIT pushbuttons not on the main fuel panel?
Fuel.a: They were added after initial design.

Fuel.q: Are the INR TANK SPLIT valves monitored by ECAM?
Fuel.a: No. They were added after initial design and are not monitored by ECAM.

Fuel.q: When are the INR TANK SPLIT pushbuttons used?
What does the amber ON light on an INR TANK SPLIT pushbutton indicate?
What does the blue SHUT light on an INR TANK SPLIT pushbutton indicate?
Which INR TANK SPLIT pushbutton lights are illuminated once the tank is split?
Fuel.a: Both the amber ON and blue SHUT lights.

Fuel.q: What is the fuel jettison rate?
What happens to the fuel pumps once the jettison QRH procedure is accomplished?
What does the crossfeed valve do when jettison begins?
Which valves open to begin fuel jettison?
Which fuel transfers begin during jettison?
Fuel.a: Trim tank to Center tank, and Outer tanks to Inner tanks.

Fuel.q: From which tanks is fuel jettisoned?
Fuel.a: Both the Inner tanks and the Center tank simultaneously.

Fuel.q: How does the crew stop a fuel jettison?
Which MCDU page entry stops the jettison automatically when reached?
Fuel.a: The fuel level input into the MCDU FUEL PRED page.

Fuel.q: At what combined Inner tank fuel quantity does jettison stop?
Fuel.a: 22,000 lbs combined Inner tank fuel quantity.

Fuel.q: Which low level sensor condition stops the jettison?
Fuel.a: Both inner tank low level sensors on one side go dry.

Fuel.q: How many conditions stop a fuel jettison?
Fuel.a: Four: crew QRH stop, MCDU FUEL PRED level reached, combined Inner 22,000 lbs, one side's low level sensors dry.

Hydraulics.q: How many Hydraulic System Monitoring Units (HSMU) control the hydraulic system?
Hydraulics.a: 1 HSMU.

Hydraulics.q: Where is the Hydraulic Architecture diagram found?
Hydraulics.a: In the QRH, OPS.08A.

Hydraulics.q: What are the 3 independent hydraulic systems?
Hydraulics.a: Green, Blue, Yellow.

Hydraulics.q: Can hydraulic fluid be transferred between the systems?
Hydraulics.a: No. Fluid cannot be transferred between the systems.

Hydraulics.q: What is normal hydraulic pressure?
What hydraulic pressure does the RAT provide?
Which is the main hydraulic system?
Hydraulics.a: Green.

Hydraulics.q: What powers the Green hydraulic system?
Hydraulics.a: 2 Engine Driven pumps plus the Ram Air Turbine (RAT).

Hydraulics.q: What is the Green system Priority Valve designed to do?
Hydraulics.a: Prioritize the flight controls in a low-pressure situation.

Hydraulics.q: Which high draw items does the Green Priority Valve cut off in low pressure?
Hydraulics.a: Emergency Generator, Nosewheel Steering, Landing Gear.

Hydraulics.q: What does the white tick mark on the SD HYD page Green reservoir signify?
Hydraulics.a: Fluid is above 17 L / 4.5 USG.

Hydraulics.q: What happens to the Green reservoir white tick mark if fluid falls below 17 L?
Hydraulics.a: It becomes two amber bars.

Hydraulics.q: Which notable brake items are on the Blue hydraulic system?
Hydraulics.a: Alternate Brakes, Parking Brake, Brake Accumulator.

Hydraulics.q: Which hydraulic system operates the Cargo Doors?
Hydraulics.a: Yellow.

Hydraulics.q: Which hydraulic systems power parts of the flight controls?
Hydraulics.a: All three: Green, Blue and Yellow.

Hydraulics.q: What pumps does each hydraulic system have?
Hydraulics.a: An Engine driven pump and an Electric Pump. Green has 2 Engine Driven Pumps.

Hydraulics.q: How many Engine Driven Pumps does the Green system have?
How long are the hydraulic electric pumps intended to be used?
Hydraulics.a: Temporary use only.

Hydraulics.q: Can the electric pumps replace the Engine driven pumps?
Hydraulics.a: No. They are for temporary use only.

Hydraulics.q: How many Pbs control each hydraulic electric pump?
Hydraulics.a: Two Pbs.

Hydraulics.q: What does the top electric pump Pb select?
Hydraulics.a: AUTO/STBY or ON.

Hydraulics.q: What does the bottom electric pump Pb do?
Hydraulics.a: Turns the pump off.

Hydraulics.q: How is an electric pump that was manually selected ON turned off?
Hydraulics.a: By returning the top Pb to AUTO.

Hydraulics.q: When should the bottom electric pump Pb OFF position be used?
Hydraulics.a: Only if directed by ECAM/QRH/FCOM.

Hydraulics.q: When does the Green electric pump come on automatically?
Hydraulics.a: When either engine has failed, or when the gear has been selected up.

Hydraulics.q: How long does the Green electric pump run after the gear is selected up?
Hydraulics.a: 25 seconds, to ensure gear retraction within the proper time.

Hydraulics.q: When does the Blue electric pump come on automatically?
Hydraulics.a: Engine 1 has failed and PRIM 1 or PRIM 3 is also inoperative.

Hydraulics.q: Why does the Blue electric pump run with Engine 1 failed and PRIM 1 or 3 inoperative?
Hydraulics.a: To assist rudder authority by ensuring at least 2 actuators are operating the rudder.

Hydraulics.q: When does the Yellow electric pump come on after an engine failure?
Hydraulics.a: Engine 2 has failed and the flap lever is not at 0.

Hydraulics.q: Why does the Yellow electric pump run after Engine 2 fails with the flap lever not at 0?
Hydraulics.a: To ensure flap retraction within the proper time.

Hydraulics.q: What happens to the Yellow electric pump when the Green electric pump runs for gear retraction after Engine 2 failure?
Hydraulics.a: It shuts off until the Green electric pump turns off.

Hydraulics.q: After Engine 2 failure, how long does the Yellow electric pump stay running?
Hydraulics.a: Until engine shutdown.

Hydraulics.q: Besides Engine 2 failure, when does the Yellow electric pump turn on automatically?
Hydraulics.a: During cargo door operation (Blue ON light illuminates automatically).

Hydraulics.q: Which valve also turns on during cargo door operation?
Hydraulics.a: The Yellow Leak Measurement Valve.

Hydraulics.q: What does the Ram Air Turbine provide?
Hydraulics.a: Redundancy to Green, backup hydraulic power to the flight controls and/or the emergency generator.

Hydraulics.q: Which engine condition automatically deploys the RAT?
Hydraulics.a: Engines 1 and 2 fail.

Hydraulics.q: Which Green and Blue condition automatically deploys the RAT?
Hydraulics.a: Green and Blue Fluid Low Level.

Hydraulics.q: Which Green and Yellow condition automatically deploys the RAT?
Hydraulics.a: Green and Yellow Fluid Low Level.

Hydraulics.q: Can the RAT be manually deployed?
Hydraulics.a: Yes. The RAT can also be manually deployed.

Hydraulics.q: Who can stow the RAT?
Hydraulics.a: Only maintenance, on the ground.

Hydraulics.q: What is the minimum RAT speed?
Hydraulics.a: 140 kts.

Hydraulics.q: What are the Leak Measurement Valves used for?
Hydraulics.a: To isolate the flight controls from hydraulic pressure.

Hydraulics.q: When does the yellow Leak Measurement Valve operate automatically?
Hydraulics.a: When the Yellow hydraulic pump activates during cargo door operation.

Ice and Rain.q: What is the normal mode for PROBE/WINDOW HEAT?
When are probes and windows automatically heated?
Ice and Rain.a: In flight, and on the ground with at least one engine running.

Ice and Rain.q: Which probe is not heated on the ground?
What does selecting the PROBE/WINDOW HEAT Pb to ON do?
Ice and Rain.a: Activates Probe/Window heat, except the TAT probes on the ground.

Ice and Rain.q: How does probe/window heat level differ between ground and flight?
Ice and Rain.a: Low heat on the ground, high heat in flight.

Ice and Rain.q: When is ENG ANTI ICE selected on?
Ice and Rain.a: When expecting potential icing. It is used as an anti-ice system.

Ice and Rain.q: How do the Engine Anti Ice valves fail with an electrical failure?
What limitations apply to the use of Engine Anti Ice?
What happens to EPR when Engine Anti Ice is selected on?
Ice and Rain.a: The EPR limit is reduced and the EPR idle is increased.

Ice and Rain.q: Does engine ignition automatically come on when Engine Anti Ice is selected on?
Ice and Rain.a: No. Only if there was an EIU failure.

Ice and Rain.q: Below what SAT is Engine Anti Ice not required in climb or cruise?
Ice and Rain.a: Below -40C SAT, due to the cold temperature.

Ice and Rain.q: When is WING ANTI ICE turned on?
Ice and Rain.a: Only when instructed by the ECAM or when there is visible ice buildup. It is a deice system.

Ice and Rain.q: Which slats are heated by WING ANTI ICE?
How do the WING ANTI ICE valves fail with an electrical failure?
Ice and Rain.a: Closed, because hot air with no cooling airflow can damage the wing composite.

Ice and Rain.q: What happens when WING ANTI ICE is activated on the ground?
Ice and Rain.a: A 30 second test occurs, then the valves close until after liftoff.

Ice and Rain.q: What happens to EPR when WING ANTI ICE is selected on?
Ice and Rain.a: The EPR limit is reduced and the EPR idle is increased.

Ice and Rain.q: What does one push of the RAIN RPLNT button do?
Ice and Rain.a: Distributes a measured quantity of fluid to the associated side.

Ice and Rain.q: When must rain repellent not be used?
What is the maximum wiper operating speed?

ECAM and Displays.q: What type of items are Level 3 ECAM Warnings?
ECAM and Displays.a: Immediate action items.

ECAM and Displays.q: What alerts accompany a Level 3 ECAM Warning?
ECAM and Displays.a: CRC sounds, Master Warning lights flash, message in red text on the E/WD.

ECAM and Displays.q: What type of items are Level 2 ECAM Cautions?
ECAM and Displays.a: Crew awareness items not requiring immediate action.

ECAM and Displays.q: What alerts accompany a Level 2 ECAM Caution?
ECAM and Displays.a: A single chime, Master Caution lights on, message in amber text on the E/WD.

ECAM and Displays.q: What type of items are Level 1 ECAM Cautions?
ECAM and Displays.a: Crew monitoring items.

ECAM and Displays.q: What alerts accompany a Level 1 Caution for loss of redundancy?
ECAM and Displays.a: No aural alerts, no Master Caution lights, message in amber text on the E/WD.

ECAM and Displays.q: How does an ECAM Advisory present on the SD?
ECAM and Displays.a: The relevant system page is called with the affected parameter pulsing green.

ECAM and Displays.q: What could an ECAM Advisory indicate?
ECAM and Displays.a: An impending failure. The system requires crew monitoring.

ECAM and Displays.q: Which QRH chart is referenced for an ECAM Advisory?
ECAM and Displays.a: The ECAM Advisory Conditions Chart, QRH 01.01A.

ECAM and Displays.q: What is Groundspeed Mini designed to protect the aircraft from?
ECAM and Displays.a: Windshear on approach, by maintaining a minimum energy level in variable wind conditions.

ECAM and Displays.q: Which speed mode must be engaged for Groundspeed Mini?
ECAM and Displays.a: Managed speed.

ECAM and Displays.q: Is Autothrust required for Groundspeed Mini?
ECAM and Displays.a: No.

ECAM and Displays.q: What do the amber double tick marks on the PFD speed tape represent?
ECAM and Displays.a: VFE Next.

ECAM and Displays.q: What does a blank tuning letter next to a NAVAID on the ND mean?
ECAM and Displays.a: The NAVAID is autotuned.

ECAM and Displays.q: What does the letter M next to a NAVAID on the ND mean?
ECAM and Displays.a: Manually tuned in the RADNAV page of the MCDU.

ECAM and Displays.q: What does the letter R next to a NAVAID on the ND mean?
ECAM and Displays.a: Physically tuned in the RMP.

ECAM and Displays.q: Does manually tuning a NAVAID affect the autotuning functions?
ECAM and Displays.a: No.

ECAM and Displays.q: Why does the ECAM inhibit some warnings and cautions during takeoff?
ECAM and Displays.a: To avoid unnecessary distraction.

ECAM and Displays.q: When does the takeoff ECAM inhibit apply?
ECAM and Displays.a: From takeoff thrust until 1500 ft or 2 minutes after liftoff.

ECAM and Displays.q: What happens to inhibited alerts once above 1500 ft or 2 minutes after liftoff?
ECAM and Displays.a: The inhibit is lifted and any inhibited alerts are displayed.

ECAM and Displays.q: Which E/WD message must be displayed for pushback?
ECAM and Displays.a: N/WS DISC.

ECAM and Displays.q: What if N/WS DISC is not displayed but the ground crew says the pin is in?
ECAM and Displays.a: Do not start the engine during pushback.

ECAM and Displays.q: What computes the GW and GW CG shown on the SD?
ECAM and Displays.a: The FCMC, using the input ZFW and the actual position of the fuel.

ECAM and Displays.q: Where are GW and GW CG displayed?
ECAM and Displays.a: In green on the bottom right of the SD.

ECAM and Displays.q: When is the GW CG displayed in red on the SD?
ECAM and Displays.a: When the Flight Envelope portion of the FMGEC detects an out of limit CG.

ECAM and Displays.q: What are the white messages under MAINTENANCE on the STATUS page?
ECAM and Displays.a: Class 2 Maintenance messages, requiring no action by the flight crew.

ECAM and Displays.q: What does the ECAM SWITCHING DMC knob select?
ECAM and Displays.a: Which DMC supplies data to the E/WD and SD.

ECAM and Displays.q: With ECAM SWITCHING in AUTO, which DMC takes over if DMC 3 fails?
ECAM and Displays.a: DMC 1.

ECAM and Displays.q: What does the ECAM/ND switch do?
ECAM and Displays.a: Transfers the SD to either the Captains or First Officers ND.

ECAM and Displays.q: What does the ECAM/ND switch transfer if both the E/WD and SD display units have failed?
ECAM and Displays.a: The E/WD to the ND.

ECAM and Displays.q: What does the EFIS DMC SWITCHING selector choose?
ECAM and Displays.a: Which DMC supplies data to the respective PFD and ND.

ECAM and Displays.q: What does the Engine position of the EFIS mode select switch display?
ECAM and Displays.a: The engine portion of the E/WD on the ND.

ECAM and Displays.q: What does the LS button display?
ECAM and Displays.a: The localizer and glide slope scales on the PFD.

ECAM and Displays.q: For which approaches is the LS button used?
ECAM and Displays.a: Only approaches utilizing a localizer: ILS, LOC, LDA.

ECAM and Displays.q: For which approaches must the LS button be off?
ECAM and Displays.a: Approaches not utilizing a localizer: RNAV, VOR, NDB.

ECAM and Displays.q: What can a Display Unit (DU) failure look like?
ECAM and Displays.a: Blank screen with amber "Invalid Display Unit", blank screen with amber "F", or a distorted display.

ECAM and Displays.q: Is a failed Display Unit recoverable?
ECAM and Displays.a: No. The DU is not recoverable.

ECAM and Displays.q: Which displays does DMC 1 provide data to?
ECAM and Displays.a: The Captains PFD and ND.

ECAM and Displays.q: Which displays does DMC 2 provide data to?
ECAM and Displays.a: The First Officers PFD and ND.

ECAM and Displays.q: Which displays does DMC 3 provide data to?
ECAM and Displays.a: The E/WD and SD.

ECAM and Displays.q: How does a DMC failure appear on the associated DUs?
ECAM and Displays.a: "Invalid Data" in amber. The DUs can be recovered by switching DMC.

ECAM and Displays.q: What happens if the E/WD DU fails?
ECAM and Displays.a: The data automatically switches to the SD.

ECAM and Displays.q: Does the SD automatically switch locations if its DU fails?
ECAM and Displays.a: No.

ECAM and Displays.q: How can SD data be displayed after the SD DU fails?
ECAM and Displays.a: ECAM/ND XFR to the Captains or FOs ND, or press and hold a systems button over the E/WD.

ECAM and Displays.q: Which DMCs can ECAM SWITCHING manually select as source for the E/WD and SD?
ECAM and Displays.a: DMC 1 or 2.

ECAM and Displays.q: What does the TO CONFIG Pb simulate?
ECAM and Displays.a: The application of takeoff power, to test if the aircraft is configured for takeoff.

ECAM and Displays.q: Which items does the TO CONFIG test check?
ECAM and Displays.a: Slats/Flaps, Pitch Trim, Rudder Trim, Speed Brakes, Brake Temperatures, Doors.

ECAM and Displays.q: Which two monitored items are not checked by the TO CONFIG test?
ECAM and Displays.a: Parking Brake and Thrust not set.

ECAM and Displays.q: What does EMER CANC do to a Warning?
ECAM and Displays.a: Silences it while the failure continues and extinguishes Master Warning lights. The ECAM message remains.

ECAM and Displays.q: What does EMER CANC do to a Caution?
ECAM and Displays.a: Cancels it for the remainder of the flight and brings up the Status page showing "Cancelled Caution".

ECAM and Displays.q: How is a cancelled Caution restored?
ECAM and Displays.a: Hold RCL for more than 3 seconds.

ECAM and Displays.q: In which cases would EMER CANC be used?
ECAM and Displays.a: To move a MEL item ECAM off the Status page, or to cancel nuisance repeating on/off Cautions.

ECAM and Displays.q: Which ECAM control panel keys are hardwired and still function if the panel fails?
ECAM and Displays.a: CLR, STS, RCL, EMER CNCL, ALL.

ECAM and Displays.q: When do the recorders start automatically?
ECAM and Displays.a: On the ground for 5 minutes after power up, on the ground after first engine start, and in flight.

ECAM and Displays.q: How long do the recorders run automatically after power up on the ground?
ECAM and Displays.a: 5 minutes.

ECAM and Displays.q: What does the RCDR GND CTL Pb do?
ECAM and Displays.a: Energizes the recorders during the preflight.

ECAM and Displays.q: Why is the CHRONO started at the beginning of the takeoff roll?
ECAM and Displays.a: To allow monitoring of engine thrust limitations.

ECAM and Displays.q: What is the engine thrust time limit at 900° in normal operations?
ECAM and Displays.a: 5 minutes.

ECAM and Displays.q: What is the engine thrust time limit at 900° if an engine has failed?
ECAM and Displays.a: 10 minutes.

Landing Gear.q: How is the landing gear normally controlled and operated?
Landing Gear.a: Electrically controlled and hydraulically operated using the green hydraulic system.

Landing Gear.q: How is the gear controlled and operated during gravity extension?
Landing Gear.a: Electrically controlled and mechanically operated.

Landing Gear.q: Can the gear be retracted normally after gravity extension if green pressure is available?
Landing Gear.a: Yes. Retract by normal methods after resetting the gravity extension switch.

Landing Gear.q: What must be done with the gravity extension switch before a normal retraction?
Landing Gear.a: Move it to RESET, then to OFF.

Landing Gear.q: How many Landing Gear Control and Interface Units (LGCIUs) control the gear system?
Landing Gear.a: Two.

Landing Gear.q: Which LGCIU powers the Landing Gear Indicator Panel next to the gear handle?
Landing Gear.a: LGCIU 1.

Landing Gear.q: What does red UNLK on the Landing Gear Indicator Panel mean?
Landing Gear.a: The gear is not in the selected position.

Landing Gear.q: What does a green triangle on the Landing Gear Indicator Panel mean?
Landing Gear.a: The gear is down and locked.

Landing Gear.q: Which LGCIUs power the two triangles per gear on the SD WHEEL page?
Landing Gear.a: Left triangle LGCIU 1, right triangle LGCIU 2.

Landing Gear.q: How many SD WHEEL page triangles per gear are needed to show down and locked?
Landing Gear.a: Only one.

Landing Gear.q: When does the Red Arrow next to the landing gear handle come on?
Landing Gear.a: At 750 ft RA if the gear is not downlocked with Flaps 2, 3, or FULL.

Landing Gear.q: What activates automatic braking?
Landing Gear.a: Ground spoiler deployment.

Landing Gear.q: Below what speed will the autobrakes not engage during an RTO?
Landing Gear.a: Below 72 kts, because the ground spoilers do not deploy until 72 kts.

Landing Gear.q: When do the autobrakes activate in LOW?
Landing Gear.a: 1 second after the ground spoilers deploy, following gear touchdown with Thrust Levers IDLE.

Landing Gear.q: When do the autobrakes activate in MED?
Landing Gear.a: When the ground spoilers deploy, following gear touchdown with Thrust Levers IDLE.

Landing Gear.q: When during taxi may the autobrakes be armed to MAX?
Landing Gear.a: Only after the flight control check.

Landing Gear.q: Why not arm autobrakes MAX before the flight control check?
Landing Gear.a: The rising spoilers during the check could activate the autobrakes.

Landing Gear.q: What does the DECEL light on the autobrake Pbs mean?
Landing Gear.a: Only that the aircraft is slowing at the programmed rate, not that the brakes are slowing it.

Landing Gear.q: What is the normal landing autobrake setting?
Landing Gear.a: LOW.

Landing Gear.q: When should autobrakes MED be used?
Landing Gear.a: For short or contaminated runways.

Landing Gear.q: When are autobrakes MAX used?
Landing Gear.a: Only for takeoff.

Landing Gear.q: What is the normal position of the A/SKID and N/W STRG switch?
Landing Gear.a: ON for normal operations.

Landing Gear.q: Which hydraulic system powers the brakes when A/SKID and N/W STRG is switched OFF?
Landing Gear.a: The Blue system, switched over from the Green system.

Landing Gear.q: Is antiskid available with A/SKID and N/W STRG switched OFF?
Landing Gear.a: No. Antiskid is deactivated.

Landing Gear.q: What happens to nosewheel steering when A/SKID and N/W STRG is switched OFF?
Landing Gear.a: Nosewheel steering is lost.

Landing Gear.q: Where is braking pressure displayed when A/SKID and N/W STRG is switched OFF?
Landing Gear.a: On the triple indicator.

Landing Gear.q: What second function does the A/SKID and N/W STRG switch serve?
Landing Gear.a: A computer reset. Check the QRH reset table on 02.02E.

Landing Gear.q: How many different methods of braking does the aircraft have?
Landing Gear.a: Four.

Landing Gear.q: Which hydraulic system powers normal brakes?
Landing Gear.a: The Green system.

Landing Gear.q: Which hydraulic system powers alternate brakes, with or without A/SKID?
Landing Gear.a: The Blue system.

Landing Gear.q: What powers the Parking Brake?
Landing Gear.a: The Blue system and the Accumulator.

Landing Gear.q: What holds the aircraft when it is parked with the engines off?
Landing Gear.a: Accumulator pressure.

Landing Gear.q: Why is Engine 1 normally started first?
Landing Gear.a: The Blue hydraulic pump is on Engine 1. It recharges the accumulator and pressurizes the parking brake.

Landing Gear.q: What does the top scale of the triple indicator display?
Landing Gear.a: Accumulator pressure.

Landing Gear.q: What does the amber scale on the top of the triple indicator indicate?
Landing Gear.a: The forbidden range. Recharge the accumulator using the blue hydraulic system.

Landing Gear.q: Where must accumulator pressure read during preflight to ensure the Parking Brake holds the aircraft?
Landing Gear.a: In the green band.

Landing Gear.q: What does the bottom scale of the triple indicator display?
Landing Gear.a: Blue system pressure delivered to the brakes.

Landing Gear.q: What does the green band on the bottom scale of the triple indicator indicate?
Landing Gear.a: The normal braking range.

Landing Gear.q: What positions can the Parking Brake valve take?
Landing Gear.a: Open or closed only, there is no in between.

Landing Gear.q: Is brake pedal pressure required to set the Parking Brake?
Landing Gear.a: No. No pressure on the brake pedals is required.

Landing Gear.q: How long can the accumulator hold the Parking Brake?
Landing Gear.a: 12 hours.

Landing Gear.q: What braking technique does the LOSS OF BRAKING memory item procedure call for?
Landing Gear.a: Short and successive applications to stop the aircraft.

Landing Gear.q: How many full brake applications will the accumulator provide at least?
Landing Gear.a: At least 7 full brake applications.

Landing Gear.q: Why delay braking to as low a speed as possible during a LOSS OF BRAKING?
Landing Gear.a: To avoid tire burst.

Navigation.q: What does the ATT HDG switch allow?
Navigation.a: IR 3 to replace IR 1 or IR 2.

Navigation.q: What is lost when an IR fails?
Navigation.a: Attitude and heading information as well as the map.

Navigation.q: What does the AIR DATA switch allow?
Navigation.a: ADR 3 to replace ADR 1 or ADR 2.

Navigation.q: What data is lost when an ADR fails?
Navigation.a: Airspeed and altitude data.

Navigation.q: What does the FM switch allow?
Navigation.a: Switching to the healthy FM in the event of FM failure.

Navigation.q: How can NAVAIDS be tuned in Back up Navigation after both FMs fail?
Navigation.a: Using the Nav function on the RMPs.

Navigation.q: Which MCDU keys still function in Back up Navigation?
Navigation.a: Only the corner keys (DIR, PROG, FPLN).

Navigation.q: How must the crew navigate in Back up Navigation?
Navigation.a: Use HDG/TRACK. NAV mode is inoperative.

Navigation.q: Does the MCDU retain the flight plan after both FMs fail?
Navigation.a: Yes. The MCDU continuously memorizes the flight plan.

Navigation.q: Do the radios still function in Back up Navigation?
Navigation.a: Yes. Radios still function normally.

Navigation.q: What does the AUDIO switch allow?
Navigation.a: The Captain or FO to utilize ACP 3 in case of ACP 1 or 2 failure.

Navigation.q: Which ADIRS rotary switch position is used for normal operations?
Navigation.a: NAV.

Navigation.q: What does the ADIRS rotary switch ATT position provide?
Navigation.a: Only attitude and heading information.

Navigation.q: How often must the heading be updated through the MCDU in ATT mode?
Navigation.a: Every 10 minutes.

Navigation.q: What does the ADIRS rotary switch OFF position do?
Navigation.a: Shuts off the entire ADIRU (both IR and ADR).

Navigation.q: How can the IR and ADR be turned off separately?
Navigation.a: Using their associated Pb's.

Navigation.q: What does a flashing IR fault indicate?
Navigation.a: Attitude and heading information can be recovered in ATT mode.

Navigation.q: What does a solid IR fault indicate?
Navigation.a: The IR has failed.

Navigation.q: How many types of ADIRS alignment are there?
Navigation.a: Two, Quick Alignment and Full Alignment.

Navigation.q: What does a Quick Alignment clear?
Navigation.a: Only the groundspeed.

Navigation.q: How long does a Quick Alignment take?
Navigation.a: 30 seconds.

Navigation.q: When is a Quick Alignment used?
Navigation.a: When a full alignment is not required.

Navigation.q: What does a Full Alignment clear?
Navigation.a: Groundspeed and drift. It also captures present position.

Navigation.q: How long does a Full Alignment take?
Navigation.a: 7 to 10 minutes.

Navigation.q: Why are the ADIRS left on when leaving the aircraft?
Navigation.a: They provide fuel system information to calculate fuel density during fueling.

Navigation.q: Is an ADIRS alignment during preflight acceptable while fueling?
Navigation.a: Yes. It is the normal procedure.

Navigation.q: With IRS only navigation in RNP 10 airspace, what is the time limit from the IRS ground alignment?
Navigation.a: Less than 6.2 hours outside radio navaid coverage.

Navigation.q: With IRS only navigation in RNP 10 airspace, what is the time limit from the last FM position update?
Navigation.a: Less than 5.7 hours outside radio navaid coverage.

Navigation.q: Why does the ON BAT light illuminate momentarily when turning the ADIRS on?
Navigation.a: It is an internal power check using the aircraft batteries.

Navigation.q: What indicates the ADIRS are using the aircraft batteries for power?
Navigation.a: A horn sounds in the nose wheel well, the same horn as the APU fire horn.

Navigation.q: What is the Mix IRS position?
Navigation.a: Each FMGEC's average of the 3 IRS provided positions.

Navigation.q: How does the Mix IRS treat one IRS position with a dramatic difference?
Navigation.a: It is factored in less than the other two.

Navigation.q: What is the bias in the GPIRS position computation?
Navigation.a: The difference between the MIX IRS position and the GPIRS position, compared by each FMGEC.

Navigation.q: How does the system handle the bias?
Navigation.a: It is constantly memorized by the system.

Navigation.q: What does the system do if radio or GPIRS data is lost?
Navigation.a: Adjusts the MIX IRS position using the bias and navigates on it until data is restored.

Navigation.q: Which IR can replace IR 1 or IR 2 using the ATT HDG switch?
Navigation.a: IR 3.

Navigation.q: Which ADR can replace ADR 1 or ADR 2 using the AIR DATA switch?
Navigation.a: ADR 3.

Navigation.q: Is NAV mode available in Back up Navigation after both FMs fail?
Navigation.a: No. NAV mode is inoperative, use HDG/TRACK to navigate.

Navigation.q: Which ACP does the AUDIO switch give the Captain or FO?
Navigation.a: ACP 3, in case of ACP 1 or 2 failure.

Navigation.q: What does GPWS SYS Off inhibit?
Navigation.a: Basic GPWS Modes 1-5. It does not affect the terrain function.

Navigation.q: What information does the GPWS TERR function use?
Navigation.a: Database terrain information, operating independently of the Basic modes 1-5.

Navigation.q: When would TERR be selected off?
Navigation.a: Due to NOTAM, or runway/airport not in the database.

Navigation.q: When should GPWS G/S Mode be turned off?
Navigation.a: Only due to a failure, glideslope signal unreliable.

Navigation.q: When should GPWS Flap Mode be turned off?
Navigation.a: Only during failures requiring landing with Flaps 0-2.

Navigation.q: Why is Flap Mode off not required for a single engine landing?
Navigation.a: FLAPS 3 can be selected on the MCDU.

Navigation.q: What does the PULL UP/GPWS Pb on the forward panel do?
Navigation.a: Temporarily inhibits the glideslope MODE 5 alert.

APU.q: What action is required if LOW OIL LEVEL is displayed on the APU SD page before a ground start?
How long can the APU operate after LOW OIL LEVEL is displayed?
What is the APU starter limit?
Can APU bleed be used for Wing Anti-Ice?
What is the APU start limit altitude?
What is the maximum altitude for APU electrical use?
What is the maximum altitude for an APU start using batteries?
What is the maximum altitude for APU electrical use plus APU bleed for 1 pack?
What is the maximum altitude for engine start using APU bleed?
What is the maximum altitude for APU electrical use plus APU bleed for 2 packs?
From where can the APU be shut down outside the aircraft?
APU.a: Two locations, the Refueling Panel and the External Power Panel.

APU.q: What controls all the APU logic?
What does an APU MASTER Switch Fault mean?
What does resetting the APU MASTER Switch reset?
What happens when the APU MASTER Switch is selected ON?
APU.a: The APU page is called on the SD and the APU intake flap opens.

APU.q: When does the APU START switch engage the starter?
APU.a: When the air intake is fully open with the Master Switch ON.

APU.q: What does the APU AVAIL light mean?
APU.a: The APU is available for Electric and/or Air.

APU.q: From which 3 places is the APU supplied fuel through the trim tank transfer line?
APU.a: Left Inner Collector Tank, Trim Pipe, Trim Tank, depending on phase of flight.

APU.q: What must be maintained in the trim tank transfer line for the APU to function?
How is the APU shut down from the cockpit panel?
What does the AVAIL light do during APU cool down?
How long can APU cool down take after the MASTER Switch is turned off?
When does the ECB command an automatic APU shutdown in the air?
APU.a: Overspeed and certain critical ECB failures.

APU.q: In the air, what causes the ECB to command an automatic APU shutdown?
APU.a: Overspeed and certain critical ECB failures.

Power Plant.q: What is the active range of the Autothrust in normal operations?
Power Plant.a: From IDLE to CLIMB detents.

Power Plant.q: What is the active range of the Autothrust in single engine operations?
Power Plant.a: From IDLE to MCT detents.

Power Plant.q: What does MAN START provide?
Power Plant.a: An alternate method of engine start.

Power Plant.q: What should pilots follow when a Manual Start is required?
Power Plant.a: The Supplementary Procedures.

Power Plant.q: Are Start Fault protections available during a Manual Start?
Power Plant.a: No. The pilots must manually abort a start if there is an issue.

Power Plant.q: When is N1 Rated or N1 Degraded mode triggered?
Power Plant.a: When EPR cannot be computed by the FADEC.

Power Plant.q: What determines whether N1 Rated or N1 Degraded mode is triggered?
Power Plant.a: Which inputs to the FADEC have failed.

Power Plant.q: What do the N1 Mode Pb's allow if only one engine is affected?
Power Plant.a: Both engines selected to N1 mode to maintain similar thrust settings.

Power Plant.q: What parameter controls the engine when N1 Mode is active?
Power Plant.a: N1, not EPR.

Power Plant.q: Is A/THR available when N1 Mode is active?
Power Plant.a: No. It is lost but can be regained if only one engine is in degraded mode.

Power Plant.q: When is Alpha Floor lost in N1 Mode?
Power Plant.a: When both engines are in degraded mode.

Power Plant.q: Are Flex takeoffs allowed when dispatched in N1 mode?
Power Plant.a: No. Flex takeoffs are prohibited.

Power Plant.q: How many levels of N1 mode are there?
Power Plant.a: Two, N1 Rated Mode and N1 Degraded Mode.

Power Plant.q: What does the FADEC display in N1 Rated Mode?
Power Plant.a: N1 limits on the upper right of the E/WD. Normal engine protections still provided.

Power Plant.q: What limits are provided in N1 Degraded Mode?
Power Plant.a: None on the E/WD. The FADEC computes a N1 red line.

Power Plant.q: What does the N1 Degraded Mode red line represent?
Power Plant.a: The full forward position of the Thrust Lever.

Power Plant.q: Is the N1 Degraded Mode red line within the actual N1 limit?
Power Plant.a: No. It is beyond the actual N1 limit and can also exceed EGT limits.

Power Plant.q: With one engine in degraded mode, what does selecting the other engine's N1 Mode Pb do?
Power Plant.a: Puts it in rated mode. The displayed rated mode limits can be used for both engines.

Power Plant.q: Which chart is used when operating in N1 Degraded Mode?
Power Plant.a: The N1 Mode Thrust Control chart in the FCOM (PER-THR-N1).

Power Plant.q: What does the Engine Master Switch initiate with the ENG START selector at IGN/START?
Power Plant.a: The automatic start sequence.

Power Plant.q: What must be set before the Engine Master Switch initiates a manual start sequence?
Power Plant.a: ENG START selector at IGN/START and ENG MAN START Pb selected ON.

Power Plant.q: What three effects does selecting IGN/START on the ENG START selector have?
Power Plant.a: Brings up the Engine page on the SD, powers the FADEC, closes the Pack Flow Control Valves.

Power Plant.q: What happens to the Pack Flow Control Valves when IGN/START is selected?
Power Plant.a: They close.

Power Plant.q: What does FADEC stand for?
Power Plant.a: Full Authority Digital Engine Control.

Power Plant.q: How many Pbs on the Maintenance Panel provide power to the FADECs on the ground?
Besides the Maintenance Panel Pbs, what else powers the FADECs?
Power Plant.a: Selecting IGN/START on the ENG START selector.

Power Plant.q: What happens to the Pack valves when FADECs are powered by IGN/START?
Power Plant.a: They close, then reopen when selected back to NORM.

Power Plant.q: Why are the FADECs energized during preflight?
Power Plant.a: To check the Engine oil level.

Power Plant.q: What is the minimum engine oil quantity required?
Power Plant.a: 15 qts, or 6 qts plus estimated consumption (0.7 qt/h), whichever is higher.

Power Plant.q: What engine oil consumption rate is used for the estimate?
Do the FADECs rely on aircraft power to continue operating?
Power Plant.a: No. They have their own magnetic alternators.
